name: Kon Pring village
summary: Ride a few kilometres up Highway 24 to Kon Pring, a Mơ Nâm community village where the steep roof of the nhà rông rises over the fields and wooden houses sit under the pine. Come for the gongs, xoang dancing, weaving, and rice wine, and give it at least an hour. Skip it on a day Pa Sy and Dak Ke already fill.
heroCaption: Kon Pring village, with the nhà rông roof across the fields

notice.title: Ask before you photograph inside the nhà rông
notice.body: Ask your host or a villager first, and put the camera away if the answer is no.

body: Kon Pring is one of four community tourism villages in Kon Plông, home to Mơ Nâm families. You see it first across the fields: low houses, pine on the hills behind, and the tall roof of the nhà rông, the communal house, rising over the fields.

Walk among the stilt houses, then ask about the gongs and xoang dancing. Performances are part of a visit but keep no fixed weekly schedule, so ask that morning or when you arrive. Weaving and rice wine are the other things families show you. Stay longer than the hour if the gongs are playing.

Stay the night if you want the village after dark. Homestays are offered, with a family meal. Otherwise ride back to town for grilled chicken and lam rice. The gate opens at 05:00, so an early start before Pa Sy also works.

figures.caption: A wooden house under pine at Kon Pring
figures.alt: A wooden house and fence under tall pine at Kon Pring village

gettingThere: Kon Pring is on Highway 24 from the Mang Den town strip. Mang Den Tourism puts it about 3 km from the centre. Go Vietnam Travel and the Vietnam Tourism rural portal put it about 5 km. Hire a car or a motorbike taxi, or ride a rented motorbike.

legs.heading: From Mang Den town
legs.body: By car or motorbike on Highway 24: about 3 km by Mang Den Tourism’s count, about 5 km by Go Vietnam Travel’s and the Vietnam Tourism rural portal’s.

legs.heading: From Kon Tum city
legs.body: About 57 km up Highway 24 by car or motorbike.

legs.heading: From Pleiku airport
legs.body: About 100 km by road to Mang Den by hired car or taxi, then on to the village along Highway 24.

admissionNote: Ask the price of a homestay night or a family meal when you arrange it.
